description.narrative:
NAGAAD Network’s campaign will support sexual assault and abuse by enhancing access to GBV specialized services and prevention information in Somaliland, particularly in drought-impacted areas, to influence Somaliland Government to fight against violenceagainst women. Women in Somaliland are disproportionately affected by climate change and the increased vulnerability can mean they experiencemore violence. As part of our influencing campaign against VAW, NAGAAD Network will communicate effectively withkey stakeholders based in Somaliland for raising awareness of gender inequality, build support for policy change, and hold decision-makers accountable.
This idea will incorporate the use of the feminist influencing basket by contributing to the feminist influencing basket (FIB) to conduct a gender analysis of the issue of violence against women in Somaliland, to build a stronger network, and to develop a joint advocacy strategy on a specific issue, such as the right to education for girls, to identifykey stakeholders such as government stakeholders and to develop a plan to engage with these stakeholders.

participating-org.narrative: Nagaad is the women#s network in Somaliland, which ON has been supporting since its establishment in1997. Nagaad was formed by 32 women#s groups in Hargeisa. While it has raised its profile tremendously after 2000, with a range of advocacy and publicity actions in the media, notably around women#s political participation, it has always remained a of 32 member organisations, many of them remain weak, except for a few larger ones (some of whom are also counterparts of Oxfam Novib). Nagaad built its own office and received support from a variety of donors. Over the last four years Nagaad has elaborated a restructuring plan and a new strategic plan that involves: (a) more focus on networking instead of direct implementation; (b) admission of 15 new members from the regions of Somaliland, and working relationships with regional women#s umbrellas and professional associations. The network now has a membership of 46organisations.
